study_identification.author_journal_year: Liu et al., Progress in Neuropsychopharmacology & Biological Psychiatry, 2024
study_identification.title: Individualized functional connectome abnormalities obtained using two normative model unveil neurophysiological subtypes of obsessive compulsive disorder

study_characteristics.study_objective: Identify neurophysiological OCD subtypes by deriving individualized deviations in functional connectivity strength (FCS) using a normative modeling framework, and assess clinical differences between subtypes.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Compared clinical variables between subtypes using t-tests. Subtype 1 was slightly older (t=2.17, p=0.032) and had later age of onset (t=2.52, p=0.014) than subtype 2; no differences in education, illness duration, symptom severity, or mean FD.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Normative modeling of ROI-wise FCS uncovered two OCD subtypes with opposite deviation patterns; pooled patients showed no significant FCS abnormalities versus HCs; subtypes differed in age of onset.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using GPR-based normative models trained on HCs, individualized FCS deviation vectors (246×1) were computed. 44.44% (n=44) of OCD patients exhibited extreme negative deviations and 21.21% (n=21) extreme positive deviations in at least one region (|Z|>1.96). K-means identified two subtypes: subtype 1 (73.74%, n=73) with decreased FCS in frontal/insula/hippocampus/precentral-postcentral regions, and subtype 2 (26.26%, n=26) with increased FCS in widespread regions (Bonferroni-corrected p<0.05). When all 99 OCD patients were combined, no significant FCS abnormalities were observed. Subtype 1 was older (t=2.17, p=0.032) with later onset (t=2.52, p=0.014). Robustness analyses showed high ARI=0.91±0.08 under subsampling and consistency across parcellations (AAL).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional single-center sample; no external validation; limited clinical variables available; potential confounds such as BMI and alcohol/cigarette use not controlled; education differed between OCD and HCs.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Normative modeling applied to FCS (Brainnetome 246) with ROI-wise GPR; k-means subtyping; robustness checks via subsampling and alternate atlas; motion evaluated and controlled in group tests.

general_notes.general_notes: Brain parcellation based on Brainnetome atlas (Fan et al., 2016); correlations threshold r>0.2 before FCS; whole-brain FCS z-normalized across participants. Inconsistency noted: abstract/Table 1 report OCD N=99, methods text says 'ninety-eight'; Table 2 OCR shows subtype Ns totaling ~100 but may include OCR errors; primary conclusions unaffected.
